production.note: US model years 2010 to 2013. First: Automotive Addicts' "New Porsche 2010 911 Turbo now has 500 horsepower", which reproduces Porsche's press release, puts US sales in "January 2010"; kbb-2010-911 lists the 2010 Turbo with "500-horsepower" and direct fuel injection, and PCNA lists the first spec sheet as "2010 911 Turbo and 911 Turbo S" (pcna-technical-specifications-index). Last: kbb-2013-911 lists a 2013 Turbo ("500 horsepower @ 6,000 rpm") and says "Only the Turbo models remain on the previous (997) architecture"; PCNA's next Turbo sheet is the "2014 911 Turbo and 911 Turbo S (991)" (pcna-technical-specifications-index).

displacementL.note: 3,800 cc. Quote: "Displacement 3800 cc". Same on the 2011 sheet.

aspiration.note: "2 turbochargers with variable turbine geometry (VTG), boost-pressure control and VarioCam Plus valve control"

fuel.note: Inferred from the spec sheet's engine description; no hybrid system.

transmission.note: "a standard six-speed manual transmission or Porsche's excellent PDK twin-clutch seven-speed transmission". Porsche's sheets list "Manual PDK" with six forward ratios for the manual and seven for PDK. The reproduced press release (automotiveaddicts-2010-911-turbo): "seven-speed PDK Doppelkupplungsgetriebe". DCT is Porsche PDK.

powerHp.note: Quote: "500 hp @ 6000 rpm" (911 Turbo and 911 Turbo Cabriolet). The 2010 sheet (pcna-2010-911-turbo-specs) also gives "500 hp" for the 911 Turbo ("500 hp @ 6000-6500 rpm"), and kbb-2013-911 gives "500 horsepower @ 6,000 rpm" for 2013.

weightLb.note: Coupe with the 6-speed manual. Quote: "Curb Weight Manual PDK Manual PDK" / "3461 lbs 3516 lbs 3627 lbs 3682 lbs" under the columns "911 Turbo | 911 Turbo Cabriolet". PDK coupe 3,516 lb. The 2010 sheet (pcna-2010-911-turbo-specs) prints the same four figures for the 911 Turbo, beside 3,494 / 3,660 lb for the PDK-only Turbo S coupe and cabriolet.
